title: Land the orphaned createTask role-attribution fix and sweep the remaining team.role call sites
description:
ORPHAN BYTES, filed by the governor so they land through the wrapper under an owning task rather than as a hand-written chore commit. This follows the resolution the human ruled on 2026-09-10 for the mention-timestamp orphan: file a task to own them, declare_files the paths, let the task's session land them.

WHAT IS SITTING DIRTY. Two files, modified 2026-09-12 00:35, declared by no task on the board:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts (+17/-5)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.test.ts (+30)

I verified the work before filing rather than assuming it was junk:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean
- `npx vitest run src/tools/createTask.test.ts` passes 12/12
- The util it imports, packages/moe-daemon/src/util/workerRole.ts, is already landed on this branch in commit b0dae82 ("fix(daemon): role gates fall back to the worker-id prefix on role-less teams")

WHAT THE CHANGE DOES, and it is a real defect fix. createTask resolved the caller's role by reading `team.role` directly. The launcher registers seats into a project-named team whose `role` is null and which holds architects, workers and QA at once, so every row an architect or governor filed was stamped `createdBy: "WORKER"`. The diff's own comment cites the measurement: on moe-next, an architect-filed row landed `createdBy: "WORKER"` because team `moe-next` carries `role: null`. The fix routes through `resolveWorkerRole`, which tries the team role first and falls back to the seat's id prefix, exactly as the role-GATED tools already do. The soft fallback for an unknown or workerId-less caller is preserved.

THE SWEEP, which is why this is not purely a landing chore. Three call sites still read `state.getTeamForWorker(...)` and branch on `team.role` without the prefix fallback:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts:138
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts:451
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/enterGovernance.ts:43

Each needs a judgement, not a blanket rewrite. claimNextTask:451 picks the `roleLabel` for the "worker is online" chat line, so a wrong role there is cosmetic but misleading. enterGovernance:43 is the governor ROLE GATE — changing it widens who may govern, so it needs deliberate thought and its own test, and it must stay refusing non-governors. Decide each on its merits and say why in the plan.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER PLANS THIS: enterGovernance.ts also has a fix in flight as PR #179 (letting a purged governor re-enter through the team tombstone). Check whether that has merged before editing that file, and rebase rather than conflict.
definitionOfDone: The two orphaned files land in a commit carrying this task's Moe-Task trailer, with no hand-written chore commit and no git operation performed by the agent outside the wrapper.

createTask stamps createdBy from the caller's resolved role, proven by a test in which the caller belongs to a team whose role is null and whose id prefix is architect, and the row lands createdBy ARCHITECT rather than WORKER.
The existing soft fallback is preserved and tested: an unknown or workerId-less caller still falls back to the explicit createdBy param, then WORKER.

Each of the three remaining team.role call sites (claimNextTask.ts:138, claimNextTask.ts:451, enterGovernance.ts:43) is either converted to resolveWorkerRole or explicitly left alone with a one-line reason recorded in the completion summary.
If enterGovernance.ts is changed, a test proves a non-governor is still refused, and no new record is created for a refused caller.
npm test in packages/moe-daemon is green and npx tsc --noEmit is clean, with both commands and their results recorded in the completion verification.
taskRails: The wrapper is the only git actor: never hand-commit these paths, and never fabricate a baseline.
enterGovernance.ts:43 is a role gate. Widening who may govern is out of scope; if you touch it, prove refusal still holds.
Check whether PR #179 has merged before editing enterGovernance.ts, and rebase rather than resolve a conflict blindly.

implementationPlan.description: FINISH THE createTask FIX AND ITS TESTS. The production change is already written; your job is to confirm it is complete and that its tests actually pin the behaviour rather than passing vacuously. Required cases in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.test.ts, each asserting an exact createdBy value: a caller on a team whose role is NULL and whose worker id begins with the architect prefix lands ARCHITECT, not WORKER - this is the defect, so it must fail if the resolver call is reverted to a direct team-role read; a caller on a team that DOES carry a role gets that team role even when the id prefix disagrees, because an explicit join is the operator stating the seat's role and must win over the id; and the soft fallback is preserved in both its steps, so an unrecognised id falls back to the explicit createdBy parameter and a caller with no workerId at all still lands WORKER. That fallback chain is the compatibility guarantee for every existing caller, and a test that only covers the happy path would let someone tighten it into a refusal later. Error handling: creating a task must never fail because a role could not be resolved - attribution is metadata, and a refusal here would break task creation for any unregistered caller. If the delivered diff already covers a case, leave it alone rather than rewriting it.
implementationPlan.note: createTask FIX CONFIRMED COMPLETE; TESTS STRENGTHENED WHERE THEY WERE VACUOUS. Production change left exactly as delivered (no rewrite): `resolveWorkerRole(state, params.workerId)` replaces the direct `team?.role` read, and the soft chain `(resolvedRole && ROLE_TO_CREATED_BY[resolvedRole]) || params.createdBy || 'WORKER'` is intact — there is no throw on an unresolvable role anywhere in the handler, so creation cannot fail on attribution. Audited the four required cases against the delivered tests: (1) role-less team + architect prefix lands ARCHITECT — covered by "attributes by id prefix when the shared team carries no role", which also pins QA/GOVERNOR/WORKER on the same `role: null` team and asserts `expect(mixed.role).toBeFalsy()` so the fixture cannot silently drift into a roled team; (2) roled team beats a disagreeing prefix — covered by "lets a roled team override the id prefix" (worker-onqateam on a qa team lands QA). Both left untouched per the step instruction. (3) The fallback chain was only HALF covered and I added the missing half: the existing arm's `worker-unknown` MATCHES the `worker-` prefix, so it lands WORKER by successful resolution, not by fallback — it would keep passing if someone deleted the `|| params.createdBy` term entirely. New test "keeps both fallback steps for an id that declares no role" uses `console-1` (no known prefix, so resolveWorkerRole returns null) and asserts both steps: with an explicit createdBy it lands HUMAN, without one it lands WORKER. (4) New test "never fails creation when the role cannot be resolved" pins the error-handling requirement on state, not just on the return value — success is true AND state.getTask(id) is non-null for an unresolvable caller, so tightening attribution into a refusal breaks a test rather than breaking every unregistered caller in production. VERIFIED: npx vitest run src/tools/createTask.test.ts = 14 passed (was 12), exit 0. Edits made with the Edit tool, not sed, per the TOOL-tier attribution note in step 1. Red proof by mutation is deferred to step 5 as the plan sequences it.

implementationPlan.description: CONVERT BOTH claimNextTask SITES. Around line 451 the roleLabel for the worker-is-online chat line falls back to guessing from the requested statuses when the team has no role; route it through resolveWorkerRole first and keep the status-based guess as the last resort. That one is cosmetic but it is a one-line improvement and an announcement that names the wrong role is exactly the kind of small lie that erodes trust in the board. Around line 138 is the substantive one, and the card undersells it: that branch routes governors away from claiming toward enter_governance, so on a role-less team a governor seat falls THROUGH and claims a task - which the project's own rules say governors never do. Convert it to resolveWorkerRole. Preserve the onboarding escape the existing comment protects, and be careful about how: the current fall-through happens for a caller with no registered worker record, so keep that condition on the worker record's existence rather than on the role lookup. A seat whose id says governor but which has not registered must still fall through, because routing it to enter_governance would hand it a next action that immediately fails with a not-found refusal. Add cases to packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts: a governor-prefixed seat on a role-less REGISTERED team is routed to enter_governance rather than claiming; the same seat unregistered still falls through; a team-supplied role still wins over the prefix; and the chat line names the resolved role.
implementationPlan.note: BOTH claimNextTask SITES CONVERTED. Site ~138 (governor redirect, the substantive one): `const team = state.getTeamForWorker(id); if (team?.role === 'governor')` becomes `if (params.workerId && state.getWorker(params.workerId)) { if (resolveWorkerRole(state, params.workerId) === 'governor') {`. The onboarding escape is preserved EXACTLY, not merely approximated: teamStore.ts:44-48 shows getTeamForWorker does `state.workers.get(workerId)` first and returns null with no record, so the old fall-through was already keyed on the worker record — the explicit state.getWorker guard restates that condition rather than adding a new one, and an unregistered governor-prefixed seat still claims instead of being handed an enter_governance next action that would throw NOT_FOUND. Site ~451 (roleLabel for the worker-is-online chat line): `team?.role ?? statusGuess` becomes `resolveWorkerRole(...) ?? statusGuess`, keeping the status-based guess as the last resort for an id that declares no role. Added `import { resolveWorkerRole } from '../util/workerRole.js'`. FOUR TESTS ADDED, two of which are red against the old code: (1) "routes a governor-prefixed seat on a ROLE-LESS team to enter_governance" seeds the launcher's exact shape (team named moe-next, `expect(team.role).toBeFalsy()`) and asserts on STATE as well as routing — a claimable WORKING task sits right there and `task.assignedWorkerId` must still be null, so the test measures the defect (a governor taking work) and not just a changed string; on the old read the role is null, the seat falls through and claims. (2) "names the resolved role in the worker-is-online chat line" deliberately picks the case where the two sources DISAGREE — an architect-prefixed seat claiming statuses ['WORKING'], where the status guess says "worker" — and pins the exact line `architect-chatline is online (architect)`; a PLANNING claim would have been vacuous because the guess already answers "architect" there. The other two are guards against my own change and pass on both sides by design: (3) "still lets an UNREGISTERED governor-prefixed seat fall through to claim" asserts the task really is assigned to it, so keying the escape on the role instead of the record would fail here; (4) "lets a team-supplied role beat the id prefix in the governor redirect" puts a governor-NAMED seat on a worker-roled team and requires it to claim normally, so an operator's explicit join_team keeps meaning something. VERIFIED: npx vitest run src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts = 47 passed (was 43), exit 0; npx tsc --noEmit exit 0. Edit tool used throughout.

implementationPlan.description: CONVERT THE GOVERNANCE GATE, AND PROVE IT STILL REFUSES. The task rail says widening who may govern is out of scope, so here is the architectural judgement behind converting it anyway, which the completion summary should restate. Converting is not a widening. The resolver's own docblock states the reason: this is a workflow guard rather than a security boundary, because join_team is unauthenticated and any seat may join any team, so a seat that wants the governor role can already grant itself one with a single call. The prefix fallback therefore hands out nothing new. What the current code DOES do is refuse a genuine governor seat on the launcher's role-less project team - the gate reads a null role and rejects - and the tool's own error text betrays it by telling the caller to go join a governor team, which is the workaround for a bug. So the change makes the gate work as intended and aligns it with every other role-gated tool, which already resolve this way. Replace the direct team-role read around line 43 with resolveWorkerRole, changing nothing else about the refusal - same error helper, same message, same not-allowed code. Add cases to packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/enterGovernance.test.ts: a governor-prefixed seat on a role-less team now enters; a worker-prefixed seat on a role-less team is still REFUSED with the same code and message, and no governance record or broadcast is created for it, asserted on state rather than only on the thrown error; and an explicitly roled team still wins over the prefix. If PR 179 has not merged by now, post one short #general line naming this file and the two-line change so its author is not surprised by a conflict, then proceed.
implementationPlan.note: GOVERNANCE GATE CONVERTED; REFUSAL PROVEN INTACT ON STATE. PR #179 re-checked immediately before editing: still OPEN (mergedAt null, head moe/fix-governor-reentry), so nothing to rebase onto. Heads-up posted to #general (msg-5d2498fe81884f0387b3d3abe146e926) naming the file, the two-line change, and — because #179 swaps the same lookup for resolveEffectiveTeam to read the purge tombstone — an explicit rebase composition so its fix is not lost in the conflict: keep `team = resolveEffectiveTeam(...)` and write `const role = team?.role ?? roleFromWorkerId(id)` (roleFromWorkerId is exported from the same util), which gives tombstone > prefix, the precedence both changes want. THE CHANGE: `const team = state.getTeamForWorker(id); if (team?.role !== 'governor')` becomes `if (resolveWorkerRole(state, params.workerId) !== 'governor')`. Nothing else moved — same notAllowed helper, same operation string, same message text, same NOT_ALLOWED code, same position BEFORE the notFound check's successor code so a refused caller still reaches no mutation. The `team` local had no other reader (grep-confirmed) so it is gone rather than left unused. THE JUDGEMENT, restated for the record so a reviewer can disagree with it on the record: the task rail says widening who may govern is out of scope, and this is not a widening. workerRole.ts's docblock states it directly — this is a workflow guard, not a security boundary, because join_team is unauthenticated and any seat may join any team, so a seat that wants the governor role can already grant itself one with a single call; the prefix fallback therefore hands out nothing that was not already one call away. What the direct read DID do is refuse a genuine governor seat on the launcher's role-less project team, and the gate's own error text ("Join a governor team to govern") is the workaround for that bug. The conversion makes the gate work as intended and aligns it with every other role-gated tool. THREE TESTS ADDED (file 6 -> 9 passing): (1) "lets a governor-prefixed seat on a ROLE-LESS team enter" — the fix, red on the old read; the fixture asserts `expect(team.role).toBeFalsy()` so it cannot drift into a roled team and pass for free. (2) "still refuses a worker-prefixed seat on a ROLE-LESS team, writing nothing" — the rail's proof, asserted on STATE and not merely on the throw: instanceof MoeError, codeName exactly 'NOT_ALLOWED', message contains 'enter_governance is governor-only', AND worker status still IDLE, currentTaskId still 'task-held' (so releaseWorkerTasks never ran), with vi.spyOn on both postToGeneral and postToRoleChannel asserted not-called, so no governance record, no status flip and no broadcast exists for a refused caller. (3) "lets an explicitly roled team beat the id prefix at the gate" — a governor-NAMED seat the operator put on a worker team is refused, so an explicit join_team still decides. Pre-existing "rejects a worker without any team (defensive)" still passes unchanged: its id `orphan-1` declares no prefix role, so resolution returns null and the refusal holds. VERIFIED: npx vitest run on the three focused files = 3 files / 70 tests passed (baseline 61), exit 0; npx tsc --noEmit exit 0.

implementationPlan.note: GATED, REVIEWED, HANDED OFF. (a) GATES. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Leaving enterGovernance alone to avoid a conflict with the open PR 179 - considered seriously and rejected: the change is two lines, it is the site where the defect bites hardest since a genuine governor is refused outright, and the honest handling of a concurrent edit is a heads-up to that author rather than silently leaving a bug. The Definition of Done permits leaving a site alone with a recorded reason, so a worker who finds PR 179 merged mid-flight should rebase rather than fight it. Treating the 138 site as cosmetic like the card implies - rejected on reading it: a governor that falls through claims work it must never claim. A blanket find-and-replace of every team.role read - rejected by the card and on merit: each site has different consequences, and the gate deserved an argument rather than a sweep. Making createTask refuse when a role cannot be resolved - rejected: attribution is metadata and a refusal would break task creation for unregistered callers, so the soft fallback chain stays and is tested in both its steps.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified live on 2026-09-12. Both orphan files are still dirty and undeclared, so the adoption path is open. The resolver's docblock is the decisive document for this task and should be read before any judgement is made: it records that a seat on a role-less team resolved to no role at all, that five parent tasks once shipped with empty dependencies because the planning architect was refused, and - crucially - that this is a workflow guard rather than a security boundary, since join_team is unauthenticated and any seat may grant itself any role with one call. That single fact is what turns the governance conversion from a widening into a repair. The card also undersells claimNextTask around line 138: that branch routes governors away from claiming, so on the launcher's role-less team a governor seat falls through and claims a task, which the project's rules say governors never do. That is a behavioural defect, not a cosmetic one. The site around 451 really is cosmetic. One trap in the 138 conversion: the existing fall-through protects onboarding for a caller with no registered worker record, so the condition must stay keyed on the worker record existing, or a governor-named seat that has not registered gets routed to a tool that immediately refuses it with not-found. PR 179 was still OPEN at planning time and touches the same gate region.
planningNotes.risks: The orphan bytes are the fragile part: declare them before anything else, never hand-commit, never fabricate a baseline. Preserve the onboarding fall-through by keying it on the worker record rather than the role. Keep the team-supplied role winning over the id prefix at every converted site, or an operator's explicit join stops meaning anything. The delivered diff is not red evidence for itself, so the proof is mutation: revert each site in a scratch copy and name the failing test, and treat a site that breaks nothing as an untested site.
